attributes.body_ja:
「までだ」と「までのことだ」は、一般的（いっぱんてき）に「ただ (B) だ」や「単（たん）に (B) だ」といった意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。 ただし、この文型（ぶんけい）は仮定文（かていぶん）の中（なか）で「(B) するしかない」といった意味（いみ）で使（つか）われることが多（おお）く、話（はな）し手（て）が「自分（じぶん）には (B) 以外（いがい）の選択肢（せんたくし）がない」と理解（りかい）し、それを受（う）け入（い）れているようなニュアンスがあります。

この文型（ぶんけい）は、動詞（どうし）の辞書形（じしょけい）の後（あと）に置（お）かれます。 大抵（たいてい）は、前（まえ）の節（せつ）に「なら」が入（はい）り、文（ぶん）の終（お）わりに「までだ」が入（はい）ります。 ほとんどの場合（ばあい）、(A) には話（はな）し手（て）にとって好（この）ましくない状況（じょうきょう）が入（はい）ります。

助詞（じょし）の「まで」は「範囲（はんい）・限界（げんかい）」を示（しめ）しますが、その意味（いみ）は「までだ」にも受（う）け継（つ）がれています。実際（じっさい）、「までだ」は「(A) という悪（わる）い状況（じょうきょう）の中（なか）で、(B) ができることの限界（げんかい）である」ことを表（あらわ）しています。
attributes.body:
までだ, and までのことだ are structures that are usually translated as 'merely (B)', or 'simply (B)'. However, they are almost always used in somewhat hypothetical sentences, and translate much closer to 'one can only but (B)'. This nuance indicates a sense of resignation, or understanding on the part of the speaker that they personally have no options beyond (B).

This grammar pattern will be used following verbs in their dictionary form, and will often come at the end of a sentence that uses なら in the first clause. In this way, it will mean 'if (A), then (B) is all that can be done'. (A) will almost always be a negative situation.

Examining the standard meaning of the particle まで as signifying an extent, it can be seen that this meaning is kept in までだ, with the speaker expressing that (B) is the extent of what is possible given the negative circumstances brought about by (A).

These are essentially the same grammar pattern, with the difference in nuance coming from the verb tense. ～たまでだ is typically used to downplay a completed action, e.g. 自分の意見を述べたまでだ ('All I did was express my opinion.), while ～るまでだ generally implies the speaker will 'just do (something)' in the face of a bad situation, e.g. 誰も教えてくれないなら、自分で調べるまでだ ('If no one will teach me, I'll just look it up myself'). Both are typically used to refer to one's own actions or those of someone in one's in-group.

Both involve a limit, but the type of limit is different. それまでだ is an evaluative expression meaning “that’s the end,” used to judge that nothing more can be done if a crucial condition is lost, as in 信頼を失ったらそれまでだ (‘If you lose trust, that’s the end.’). By contrast, Vるまでだ (and までのことだ) expresses resignation, meaning “one can only but (B),” often used with なら to show that (B) is the only remaining option in a negative situation, as in 誰にも教えてもらえないなら、ネットで調べてみるまでだ (‘If no one will teach me, I’ll just have to look it up online.’).
